page: Amazon Web Services c8g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz, utilizing the Neoverse-V2 core design from the ARMv9 family. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not feature local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In multi-threaded and parallel processing benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance. Multi-core CPU stress tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation with clang all rank in the top 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached read speeds reaching 21,306.42 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 403.08 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also achieve top-tier results, with Redis SET operations reaching 355.18 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and LLM prompt processing for small models represent comparative bottlenecks, scoring in the average and weak tiers respectively.

Given its high core density and strong multi-threaded performance, the c8g.48xlarge is suited for highly parallelized compute-bound workloads. These include large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded data decompression, physics simulations, and high-throughput static web serving. The ARM-based architecture provides high resource density and compute efficiency for multi-core tasks, though workloads requiring high single-thread performance or local NVMe storage may require alternative configurations.
